title: Moving between Levels of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan
content:
A guest who wants a different level of the Keyturn Guest Protection Plan asks for a change, which is taken
onto the change request register and priced only once it is approved, so the level on the election never moves on
the strength of the request alone.

What may be changed depends on the level and on whether the trip has started. Moving up before the trip starts is
open on every level; moving up once the trip has started is open only on the levels that allow it. Moving down is
open only on the levels that allow it, and moving down once the trip has started is open on fewer levels still.

A change is priced only where the request is recorded no later than the change decision window counted forward
from the moment the guest asked for it. The decision window is counted in whole elapsed hours from the timestamp
on the change request, never in calendar days, and an hour counts only once it has fully elapsed.

An upgrade is priced on the level's proration basis. Where it is the whole trip, the difference is charged for
every day of the trip as if the new level had been chosen at the start.

A downgrade returns the level's downgrade credit percentage of the same difference and never the whole of it,
because cover already run cannot be given back; a level whose downgrade credit is nil returns nothing at all.

Cover after a change is the new level's cover for the rest of the trip and the old level's cover for the part
already run, so a loss is settled on the level in force on the day the loss happened.

## The window read as a clock

| What is read | What it is |
|---|---|
| The moment the clock starts | The timestamp on the change request, which is the moment the guest asked for the change |
| The record that proves it | The change request itself, correlated by its own reference number, read before the change is priced |
| How the time is counted | In whole elapsed hours, never in calendar days, an hour counting only once it has fully elapsed |
| The direction of the comparison | The request must be recorded no later than the window counted forward from that moment |
| The boundary | The last hour of the window is inside it |

**Hypothetical case that just satisfies the window.** A request timestamped at the top of an hour, on a level
whose decision window is 4 hours, is recorded again when 4 whole hours have elapsed. Four is not later than
four, so the change may be priced.

**Hypothetical case that just fails.** The same request, recorded when 5 whole hours have elapsed, is past the
window and the change is not priced on it.

## Clauses no longer in force

1. "Where that basis is the remaining whole days, the difference between the two levels' daily fees is charged for the days left in the trip counted from the day of the change, the day of the change itself included." — no longer in force.
2. "A change made once the trip has started carries the level's mid-trip change fee where the level has one, posted as part of the same line rather than separately." — no longer in force.

The proration bases and the mid-trip change fees recorded against the levels of the Keyturn Guest Protection
Plan remain recorded terms of those levels; the two clauses above are not applied to a change.
